security_audit.summary: Static findings were reviewed in context; the import, grid search, temp cache, URL, and Markdown backtick matches are false positives from normal scikit-learn documentation and examples. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found. The remaining content-level issue is unsafe pickle loading guidance without a trusted-source warning.

remediation.suggestion: Add a warning that pickle files can execute code, load only trusted model artifacts, and consider safer formats where appropriate.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Pickle Deserialization Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The model persistence section shows loading model.pkl with pickle.load without warning that pickle files must come from trusted sources. Loading an untrusted pickle can execute arbitrary code in the Python process.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly call pickle.load on a model file and the surrounding section does not provide a trust-boundary warning. The issue is unsafe guidance, not evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Classical machine learning projects need reliable guidance for preprocessing, model selection, and evaluation. This skill provides scikit-learn references, scripts, and workflow patterns for repeatable ML experiments.
actual_capabilities: Guides classification and regression workflows with common scikit-learn estimators.
Shows preprocessing for numeric, categorical, and missing data using pipelines.
Explains cross-validation, metric selection, grid search, and random search.
Provides reference scripts for classification pipelines and clustering analysis.
Covers clustering, dimensionality reduction, and model persistence examples.
limitations: Focuses on classical scikit-learn, not deep learning frameworks.
Examples assume users provide their own datasets and feature names.
Reference code may need adaptation for library versions and data size.
Does not replace privacy review, statistical validation, or production monitoring.

use_cases.title: Create a Baseline Classifier
use_cases.description: Build a first supervised model with preprocessing, stratified splitting, model comparison, and clear evaluation metrics.

use_cases.title: Design a Production Pipeline
use_cases.description: Combine transformers, estimators, and hyperparameter tuning into a repeatable scikit-learn workflow.

use_cases.title: Explore Unlabeled Data
use_cases.description: Compare clustering methods, evaluate cluster quality, and visualize high-dimensional datasets with PCA.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Classifier
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me build a scikit-learn classifier for my tabular dataset. Include the train test split, preprocessing steps, model choice, and evaluation metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Candidate Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare suitable scikit-learn models for my prediction task. Recommend cross-validation settings, metrics, and a concise model comparison plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Mixed-Data Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a scikit-learn Pipeline for numeric and categorical features. Include imputation, encoding, scaling, hyperparameter tuning, and leakage prevention checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an ML Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my scikit-learn workflow for data leakage, weak metrics, overfitting risk, reproducibility gaps, and unsafe model persistence practices.

output_examples.input: I need a baseline classifier for customer churn data.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline covering stratified splitting, pipeline preprocessing, model comparison, grid search, and classification metrics.

output_examples.input: I have unlabeled customer records and want segments.
output_examples.output: A clustering plan with scaling, candidate algorithms, silhouette review, and PCA-based visualization guidance.

output_examples.input: Review my planned model training process before launch.
output_examples.output: A checklist for leakage, metric choice, cross-validation design, hyperparameter scope, reproducibility, and model persistence risks.

best_practices: Put preprocessing inside Pipeline or ColumnTransformer to reduce leakage risk.
Split data before fitting scalers, imputers, encoders, or feature selectors.
Choose metrics that match the target, class balance, and business cost.
anti_patterns: Fitting preprocessing on the full dataset before train test splitting.
Reporting only accuracy for imbalanced classification problems.
Loading pickle model files from untrusted or unknown sources.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan and implement scikit-learn workflows for supervised learning, clustering, preprocessing, evaluation, tuning, and pipelines.

faq.question: Does it include runnable examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes example scripts for a classification pipeline and clustering analysis.

faq.question: Can it help prevent data leakage?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes pipelines, proper train test splitting, and fitting preprocessing only on training data.

faq.question: Does it cover deep learning?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on classical machine learning with scikit-learn.

faq.question: Can it help choose evaluation metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers classification, regression, and clustering metrics for common modeling goals.

faq.question: Is model persistence covered?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes persistence examples, but users should only load model files from trusted sources.
